title: Class Definition
description: Define a class with constructor and instance methods
code:
class Dog:
    # Class variable (shared by all instances)
    species = "Canis familiaris"
    
    # Constructor — called when object is created
    def __init__(self, name: str, age: int):
        self.name = name    # Instance variable
        self.age = age
    
    # Instance method
    def bark(self):
        return f"{self.name} says Woof!"
    
    def __str__(self):
        return f"{self.name} ({self.age} years)"

# Create instances:
dog1 = Dog("Buddy", 3)
dog2 = Dog("Max", 5)

print(dog1.bark())        # Buddy says Woof!
print(dog2.bark())        # Max says Woof!
print(dog1.species)       # Canis familiaris
print(dog1)               # Buddy (3 years)
print(type(dog1))         # <class '__main__.Dog'>

# isinstance check:
print(isinstance(dog1, Dog))  # True
print(isinstance(dog1, object))  # True (everything is object)
explanation: class defines a class. __init__ is the constructor. self refers to the instance. Class variables are shared.

title: Instance Vs Class Variables
description: Understand the difference between class and instance variables
code:
class Employee:
    # Class variable — shared by all instances
    company = "Acme Corp"
    employee_count = 0
    
    def __init__(self, name: str, salary: float):
        # Instance variables — unique per instance
        self.name = name
        self.salary = salary
        Employee.employee_count += 1  # Access class var via class
    
    def info(self):
        return f"{self.name} works at {self.company}"  # Can use self

# Create instances:
e1 = Employee("Alice", 50000)
e2 = Employee("Bob", 60000)

print(e1.company)     # Acme Corp
print(e2.company)     # Acme Corp
print(Employee.company)  # Acme Corp

# Modify class variable:
Employee.company = "New Corp"
print(e1.company)     # New Corp (changed for all)

# Instance shadowing (makes instance variable):
e1.company = "Private"  # Creates instance variable! Doesn't change class
print(e1.company)        # Private (instance variable)
print(e2.company)        # New Corp (class variable)

print(Employee.employee_count)  # 2
print(e1.employee_count)  # 2 (access via instance, falls back to class)

# Track class vars:
print(Employee.__dict__)
print(e1.__dict__)  # Only instance vars
explanation: Class variables are shared. Instance variables are per-object. Setting via instance creates a new instance var.

title: Inheritance
description: Create a class that inherits from another class
code:
class Animal:
    def __init__(self, name: str):
        self.name = name
    
    def speak(self) -> str:
        return "..."
    
    def move(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.name} moves"

class Dog(Animal):
    def __init__(self, name: str, breed: str):
        super().__init__(name)  # Call parent constructor
        self.breed = breed
    
    def speak(self) -> str:  # Override parent method
        return "Woof!"
    
    def fetch(self) -> str:  # New method
        return f"{self.name} fetches the ball"

class Cat(Animal):
    def speak(self) -> str:
        return "Meow!"

# Usage:
dog = Dog("Buddy", "Golden Retriever")
cat = Cat("Whiskers")

print(dog.speak())     # Woof! (overridden)
print(dog.move())      # Buddy moves (inherited)
print(dog.fetch())     # Buddy fetches the ball
print(cat.speak())     # Meow!

# isinstance and issubclass:
print(isinstance(dog, Dog))     # True
print(isinstance(dog, Animal))  # True (inheritance!)
print(issubclass(Dog, Animal))  # True
print(issubclass(Cat, Animal))  # True

# Type hierarchy:
print(Dog.__bases__)   # (<class '__main__.Animal'>,)
print(Animal.__subclasses__())  # [<class '__main__.Dog'>, <class '__main__.Cat'>]
explanation: Use class Child(Parent) for inheritance. super() calls the parent class. Methods can be overridden.

title: Multiple Inheritance
description: A class can inherit from multiple parent classes
explanation: Python uses C3 linearization for MRO. super() follows the MRO order. Methods from first parent take priority.

title: Magic Methods Overview
description: Special methods (dunder methods) that customize class behavior
code:
class Book:
    def __init__(self, title: str, author: str, pages: int):
        self.title = title
        self.author = author
        self.pages = pages
    
    # String representation:
    def __str__(self):
        return f"'{self.title}' by {self.author}"
    
    def __repr__(self):
        return f"Book('{self.title}', '{self.author}', {self.pages})"
    
    # Length:
    def __len__(self):
        return self.pages
    
    # Equality and comparison:
    def __eq__(self, other):
        if not isinstance(other, Book):
            return NotImplemented
        return self.title == other.title and self.author == other.author
    
    def __lt__(self, other):
        return self.pages < other.pages
    
    # Container methods:
    def __getitem__(self, key):
        if key == "title":
            return self.title
        elif key == "author":
            return self.author
        raise KeyError(key)
    
    # Callable:
    def __call__(self):
        return f"Reading {self.title}..."
    
    # Boolean:
    def __bool__(self):
        return self.pages > 0

b1 = Book("1984", "George Orwell", 328)
b2 = Book("Animal Farm", "George Orwell", 112)

print(str(b1))           # '1984' by George Orwell
print(repr(b1))          # Book('1984', 'George Orwell', 328)
print(len(b1))           # 328
print(b1 == b2)          # False
print(b2 < b1)           # True (112 < 328)
print(b1["title"])      # 1984
print(b1())              # Reading 1984...
print(bool(Book("", "", 0)))  # False

# Custom class can be used in sorting:
books = [b1, b2]
print(sorted(books))     # Sorted by pages
explanation: Magic methods (__str__, __eq__, __len__, etc.) customize behavior for built-in operations.

title: Abstract Base Class (ABC)
description: Define abstract base classes with abc module
explanation: ABCs define interfaces that subclasses must implement. Instantiation of ABCs is prevented.

title: Dataclasses
code:
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

@dataclass
class Person:
    name: str
    age: int = 0
    city: str = "Unknown"

# Auto-generated __init__:
p = Person("Alice", 30, "NYC")
print(p)               # Person(name='Alice', age=30, city='NYC')

# Auto-generated __eq__:
p2 = Person("Alice", 30, "NYC")
print(p == p2)         # True (compares all fields)

# Auto-generated __repr__:
print(repr(p))         # Person(name='Alice', age=30, city='NYC')

# Frozen (immutable) dataclass:
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Point:
    x: float
    y: float

pt = Point(3.0, 4.0)
print(pt.x)            # 3.0
# pt.x = 5.0           # FrozenInstanceError!

# Field customization:
@dataclass
class Employee:
    name: str
    salary: float = field(default=0.0, repr=False)  # Hidden in repr
    tags: list = field(default_factory=list)  # Mutable default
    id: int = field(init=False)  # Not in __init__
    
    def __post_init__(self):
        """Called after __init__."""
        self.id = hash(self.name) % 10000

e = Employee("Bob", 60000, tags=["senior"])
print(e)              # Employee(name='Bob', tags=['senior'], id=...)

# Ordered dataclass (supports sorting):
@dataclass(order=True)
class Product:
    name: str
    price: float

p1 = Product("Apple", 0.50)
p2 = Product("Banana", 0.30)
print(p1 > p2)  # True (compares by price? No, compares by first field)

# Data class inheritance:
@dataclass
class Animal:
    name: str
    sound: str

@dataclass
class Dog(Animal):
    breed: str = "Mixed"
    # Inherits name and sound, adds breed

d = Dog("Buddy", "Woof", "Golden")
print(d)  # Dog(name='Buddy', sound='Woof', breed='Golden')
explanation: @dataclass auto-generates __init__, __repr__, __eq__, and __hash__. Use field() for customization.

title: Slots
description: Reduce memory usage by preventing __dict__ creation
code:
class Point:
    __slots__ = ('x', 'y')  # Only these attributes allowed
    
    def __init__(self, x: float, y: float):
        self.x = x
        self.y = y

p = Point(3.0, 4.0)
print(p.x)         # 3.0
print(p.y)         # 4.0

# No __dict__:
# print(p.__dict__)  # AttributeError: 'Point' has no attribute '__dict__'

# Cannot add new attributes:
# p.z = 5.0  # AttributeError!

# Memory comparison:
class PointDict:
    def __init__(self, x, y):
        self.x = x
        self.y = y

class PointSlots:
    __slots__ = ('x', 'y')
    def __init__(self, x, y):
        self.x = x
        self.y = y

import sys
pd = PointDict(1, 2)
ps = PointSlots(1, 2)
print(sys.getsizeof(pd))   # ~56 bytes (plus __dict__ overhead)
print(sys.getsizeof(ps))   # ~48 bytes (no __dict__)

# Slots with inheritance:
class Base:
    __slots__ = ('a',)

class Derived(Base):
    __slots__ = ('b',)  # Must define slots again
    
    def __init__(self, a, b):
        self.a = a
        self.b = b

# When to use __slots__:
# · Creating millions of instances
# · Memory is critical
# · Want to restrict attribute creation
# 
# Drawbacks:
# · Prevents __dict__ creation
# · Multiple inheritance with slots is complex
# · Cannot add attributes dynamically
explanation: __slots__ restricts attribute creation and reduces memory overhead by eliminating __dict__ per instance.

title: Enums
description: Create enumerations of symbolic names bound to unique values
code:
from enum import Enum, auto, IntEnum, unique

class Color(Enum):
    RED = 1
    GREEN = 2
    BLUE = 3

print(Color.RED)              # Color.RED
print(Color.RED.name)         # 'RED'
print(Color.RED.value)        # 1
print(type(Color.RED))        # <enum 'Color'>
print(isinstance(Color.RED, Color))  # True

# Iteration:
for color in Color:
    print(f"{color.name}: {color.value}")

# Comparison:
print(Color.RED == Color.RED)        # True
print(Color.RED is Color.RED)        # True
print(Color.RED == Color.BLUE)       # False
print(Color.RED == 1)                # False (enum != int)

# auto() assigns increasing values:
class Status(Enum):
    PENDING = auto()  # 1
    ACTIVE = auto()   # 2
    INACTIVE = auto() # 3
    BANNED = auto()   # 4

print(Status.ACTIVE.value)  # 2

# Unique values decorator:
@unique
class Direction(Enum):
    NORTH = 1
    EAST = 2
    SOUTH = 3
    WEST = 4
    # NORTH = 5  # ValueError: duplicate values!

# IntEnum: behaves like int
class Priority(IntEnum):
    LOW = 1
    MEDIUM = 5
    HIGH = 10

print(Priority.HIGH > Priority.LOW)  # True (int comparison!)
print(Priority.HIGH == 10)           # True

# StrEnum (Python 3.11+):
# from enum import StrEnum

# Aliases (same value, different name):
class Animal(Enum):
    CAT = 1
    DOG = 2
    KITTY = 1  # Alias for CAT

print(Animal(1))       # Animal.CAT (first one)
print(Animal["KITTY"]) # Animal.KITTY

# Methods in enums:
class Planet(Enum):
    MERCURY = (3.303e23, 2.4397e6)
    VENUS = (4.869e24, 6.0518e6)
    EARTH = (5.976e24, 6.37814e6)
    
    def __init__(self, mass, radius):
        self.mass = mass
        self.radius = radius
    
    @property
    def surface_gravity(self):
        G = 6.674e-11
        return G * self.mass / (self.radius * self.radius)

print(Planet.EARTH.surface_gravity)  # 9.802...

# Enum member access:
color = Color(2)        # By value
print(color)            # Color.GREEN

color2 = Color["BLUE"]  # By name
print(color2)           # Color.BLUE
explanation: Enum creates symbolic constants. auto() for automatic values. @unique for no duplicates. IntEnum for int compatibility.

title: Operator Overloading
description: Customize operators (+, -, *, etc.) for your class
explanation: Override __add__, __sub__, __mul__ etc. to customize operators. __rmul__ handles reverse operations.

title: Context Manager (with statement)
description: Create custom context managers for resource management
code:
class ManagedFile:
    def __init__(self, filename: str, mode: str = "r"):
        self.filename = filename
        self.mode = mode
    
    def __enter__(self):
        """Called when entering 'with' block. Returns the resource."""
        self.file = open(self.filename, self.mode)
        return self.file
    
    def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb):
        """Called when exiting 'with' block (even on exception)."""
        self.file.close()
        # Return False to propagate exception, True to suppress
        if exc_type is not None:
            print(f"An error occurred: {exc_val}")
        return False  # Don't suppress exceptions

# Usage:
with ManagedFile("test.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("Hello, World!")
# File is automatically closed

# Using contextlib for simpler context managers:
from contextlib import contextmanager

@contextmanager
def managed_file(filename: str, mode: str = "r"):
    f = open(filename, mode)
    try:
        yield f  # Value returned to 'as' target
    finally:
        f.close()  # Cleanup runs even on exception

with managed_file("test.txt", "r") as f:
    print(f.read())

# Context manager for timing:
import time

@contextmanager
def timer(description: str = ""):
    start = time.perf_counter()
    yield
    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start
    print(f"{description} took {elapsed:.4f}s")

with timer("Heavy computation"):
    sum(range(10_000_000))

# Context manager for temporary directory:
import tempfile
import shutil
from pathlib import Path

@contextmanager
def temp_dir():
    tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    try:
        yield Path(tmp)
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(tmp)

with temp_dir() as tmp:
    (tmp / "test.txt").write_text("Hello")
    print(list(tmp.iterdir()))  # [WindowsPath('.../test.txt')]
# Directory cleaned up
explanation: __enter__ returns the resource, __exit__ handles cleanup. @contextmanager simplifies creation.

title: Descriptors
explanation: Descriptors (__get__/__set__) control attribute access. Used internally by @property, @classmethod, @staticmethod.

title: Composition Vs Inheritance
explanation: Inheritance = IS-A (Dog is an Animal). Composition = HAS-A (Car has an Engine). Favor composition.

title: Mixin Pattern
description: Use mixins to compose reusable behaviors via multiple inheritance
explanation: Mixins are small reusable classes that add specific functionality via multiple inheritance.

title: Metaclass Basics
description: Metaclasses are classes of classes — they control class creation
explanation: Metaclasses control class creation and behavior. Use sparingly — dataclasses, descriptors often suffice.
